description:
1. We all have free will, including the angels. Can God's angels sin? 

2. Why was David wrong to count the Israelites in 1 Chronicles? 

3. Can you please explain 1 Timothy 4: 3-5? Does this mean we can eat any type of flesh as long as we bless or pray over it? I know about the clean meats in Deuteronomy 14. I am confused; it seems to be a contradiction.  

4. My extended family gets together each year around Christmas time. They understand that I'm an Adventist, but the event is usually on Saturday. Should I attend or not? I feel that if I don't attend, I'll miss opportunities to share my faith, but at the same time, I want to keep the Sabbath holy. Should we attend parties and social gatherings on the Sabbath?

5. After Cain left the presence of God in Genesis Chapter 4, who gave birth to the woman that he married? Were there other humans in the world apart from Adam, his wife, and Cain? Who gave birth to Cain’s wife?

6. Do the fallen angels have the same powers, abilities, and knowledge as the Angels in Heaven? Do fallen angels have the same powers as heavenly angels?
 
7. If there was no sin in the beginning, why did God ask Cain and Abel to bring him a sacrifice? 

8. From a Baptist sister curious about Sabbath: How should I properly keep the Sabbath holy? What activities should I avoid on this day, and how can I truly delight in it as God intended? 

9. I often hear people say that everyone is a child of God. I don't believe that because I know some people choose not to be his child. If everyone were a child of God, wouldn't that mean that everyone would be saved? Is everyone a child of God?

10. Why did Jesus convert Saul, who later switched to Paul, but not convert Caiaphas as well? Why did Jesus convert Saul but not Caiaphas?

11. Do you have to be baptized in water to be saved? I would love to be baptized in water. Where I live, there isn't any church that I like or attend, so I watch Christian TV and read the Bible every day. I believe that Jesus died for our sins and was resurrected by God.  

12. I have hurt someone who has since passed away. I had the opportunity to ask for forgiveness, but I didn’t—out of shame, and because I took the situation for granted. Now, whenever I think of this person, it deeply hurts me. I often reflect on this in relation to judgment and the salvation of my soul. I have prayed and asked God to forgive me, but I never asked forgiveness from the person themselves. Will God forgive me?  I hurt someone who has died and never asked for forgiveness. Will God forgive me?
